summary: Hyoscyamine is an FDA-approved belladonna-alkaloid antimuscarinic used to relax GI and urinary smooth muscle and to reduce secretions in conditions such as irritable bowel syndrome, GI spasm/hypermotility, and as a drying agent. Immediate-release doses are 0.125-0.25 mg every 4 hours as needed (max 1.5 mg/day); extended-release is 0.375-0.75 mg every 12 hours. Anticholinergic effects (dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation, urinary retention) limit use, and it is contraindicated in glaucoma and obstructive disease.
indications: Adjunctive control of GI disorders due to spasm (irritable bowel syndrome, spastic/functional GI disorders)
Treatment of peptic ulcer disease and to reduce GI motility/secretion (adjunct)
Control of gastric/intestinal hypermotility, biliary and renal colic, and bladder spasm
As a drying agent to reduce salivary, bronchial and other secretions; adjunct in some forms of partial heart block from vagal activity

dosage.d: Reduced weight-based dosing per product labeling

admin: Take 30-60 minutes before meals and at bedtime for spasm control
Place sublingual tablets under the tongue; allow orally disintegrating tablets to dissolve
Swallow extended-release tablets whole - do not crush or chew
Maintain hydration and avoid overheating, as sweating is reduced
Use the lowest effective dose, especially in the elderly
moa: Hyoscyamine is the levorotatory isomer of atropine and competitively blocks acetylcholine at postganglionic muscarinic receptors. This inhibits parasympathetic effects on smooth muscle and glands, reducing GI and genitourinary smooth-muscle tone and motility and decreasing salivary, bronchial, gastric and other secretions.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to hyoscyamine or belladonna alkaloids
Obstructive uropathy (e.g., bladder neck obstruction from prostatic hypertrophy)
Obstructive GI disease (pyloric stenosis, paralytic ileus, severe ulcerative colitis/toxic megacolon)
relative: Coronary heart disease, tachyarrhythmias, heart failure

preg: There are limited data; hyoscyamine crosses the placenta. Use during pregnancy only if clearly needed and the benefit justifies any potential risk.
lact: Trace amounts of hyoscyamine may pass into breast milk, and anticholinergics can suppress lactation. Use with caution and observe the infant for anticholinergic effects.
renal: Hyoscyamine is partly excreted renally; impairment may prolong its effect. Use cautiously and reduce the dose as needed.
hepatic: Use with caution in hepatic impairment; titrate to the lowest effective dose.

major: Potassium chloride (solid oral) - delayed GI transit increases GI ulceration risk
Other anticholinergics (antihistamines, TCAs, antipsychotics) - additive anticholinergic toxicity
Pramlintide - additive slowing of gastric emptying
moderate: Antacids - reduce hyoscyamine absorption; separate dosing
interactions.food: Take before meals; antacids and food can reduce absorption.
interactions.alcohol: Avoid alcohol; additive drowsiness and CNS impairment.
interactions.diagnostics: Delays gastric emptying (may affect gastric studies); can cause mydriasis affecting eye exams.

monitoring: Anticholinergic side effects (dry mouth, vision, bowel/bladder function)
Heart rate and rhythm in cardiac patients
Mental status, particularly in elderly patients
counsel: Take 30-60 minutes before meals for best effect on cramps
Dry mouth, blurred vision and constipation are common - use sugar-free gum/fluids and report severe symptoms
Avoid getting overheated; you sweat less while on this drug
Do not drive until you know how it affects your alertness and vision
Avoid alcohol and tell your doctor about eye pressure problems or trouble urinating
pk: Store at 20-25 C (68-77 F); protect from light/moisture
pearls: Hyoscyamine is FDA-approved (unlike some belladonna combinations) - the l-isomer of atropine
Classic anticholinergic cautions: avoid in narrow-angle glaucoma and obstructive uropathy/GI disease
Elderly are especially prone to confusion, retention and falls - use the lowest dose
Reduces sweating; counsel on heat-stroke risk in hot weather
Sublingual and orally disintegrating forms allow faster onset for acute spasm
missed: For scheduled dosing, take the missed dose when remembered; if near the next dose, skip it. For as-needed use, take only when symptoms occur. Do not double up, and do not exceed 1.5 mg in 24 hours.
overdose: Overdose produces the anticholinergic toxidrome: dilated pupils, hot dry flushed skin, fever, urinary retention, tachycardia, delirium, hallucinations and possibly seizures, respiratory failure and coma. Treatment is supportive with cooling, fluids, benzodiazepines for agitation/seizures; physostigmine may reverse severe central anticholinergic toxicity under monitoring.
